source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Infer that a person is unwell when symptoms or signs show that the body or mind is not working normally.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The healthy person who is tired after ordinary exercise is unwell.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Dizziness causes the underlying organ malfunction.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A person whose mind is not functioning normally is still well if their body functions normally.

intelligence.enrichment: Being unwell means something in the body or mind may not be working as it should; a disease affects the normal working of the body or mind. When one or more organs, organ systems, or the mind stop functioning properly, symptoms or signs can appear. The learner correctly applies this rule: Being unwell means something in the body or mind may not be working as it should; a disease affects the normal working of the body or mind. A person is unwell only when the discomfort is severe; fever, rash, pain, or dizziness can be ignored if the person keeps working.
